source.title: On the Sample Complexity of One Hidden Layer Networks with Equivariance, Locality and Weight Sharing

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Provides theoretical bounds and numerical experiments on equivariance group size and frequency locality, and reports how these relate to measured generalization error and test accuracy. These bear on V3's architectural-bias topic through a different setup and analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own numerical results for bound-versus-generalization-error correlations and for frequency cutoffs. Bounds, propositions, and results cited from other work are not empirical rows. The experiments use equivariant one-hidden-layer models on transformed binary MNIST/CIFAR10 tasks; they do not compare convolutional and fully connected models trained from scratch.
record.test_reason: The study derives complexity bounds and measures generalization gaps in equivariant networks. It does not establish V3's lower test error for convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch. Bounds improved by locality and correlations with generalization gaps measure different outcomes from that comparison. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the numerical findings but omits the main theoretical conclusions: mostly dimension-free norm-based bounds for single-hidden-layer equivariant networks, comparable guarantees from suitable non-equivariant weight sharing, and additional potential gains from local filters subject to a spatial–frequency locality trade-off. The authors acknowledge limitations for deeper networks and uncertainty about the optimal group size.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses statistical learning theory bounds and experiments on one-hidden-layer equivariant models with fixed random equivariant feature projections, transformed binary tasks, and frequency cutoffs. It does not reproduce the original convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured trends vary with equivariance group, maximum filter frequency, and training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: The norm term M1M2/√m correlates with measured generalization gaps across groups and sample sizes on transformed binary MNIST and CIFAR10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Norm-based complexity measures can track generalization gaps in these shallow equivariant networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower frequency cutoffs generally reduce generalization gaps, while higher cutoffs can improve test accuracy; the trade-off depends on sample size and saturation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Frequency restrictions trade expressivity against generalization gap in shallow equivariant classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Propositions 6.1 and 7.1 give comparable bounds for suitable non-equivariant weight sharing and an additional bound improvement from spatial locality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitable weight sharing and local filters can tighten norm-based generalization guarantees under the stated assumptions.

record.problems: The numerical experiments are on transformed binary MNIST and CIFAR10 tasks using a fixed random D32-steerable projection, rather than standard image classifiers trained from scratch. The text reports trend correlations and qualitative results, not exact per-condition values. No direct fully connected comparison is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results identified. Figure 2–4 plots include trends whose prose descriptions are recorded above; no numeric values were reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy alongside natural-label generalization.
Test error under widening beyond zero training error; dimension-free bounds do not establish this training outcome.

Convolutional versus fully connected test error under training from scratch, the contribution of spatial local connectivity to that difference, and sparse-local or convolution-initialized fully connected comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epochs and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, dataset-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against norm and margin measures.
Removal of memorized versus random examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Generalization error here denotes the test–training gap, which must be distinguished from held-out error or accuracy. A smaller gap can accompany worse test accuracy. The existing V3 limits_scope labels should be removed because these results do not test that version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
No fully connected comparison or local-connection learning experiment; the experiments study group equivariance and frequency cutoffs in a transformed binary classification setup.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparison.
Large versus small batch sizes and recipe changes.
Dropout intervention and its interaction with dataset size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.

rows.value: For each dataset size, increasing frequency improves test performance until a saturation point; beyond it, increased frequencies mostly lead to increased generalization error. rows.note: The authors describe a trade-off between generalization error and test performance, with behavior changing by dataset size and frequency.
